historical_record.description: The Recreation and Park Commission approved a professional services agreement with Francisco J. Centurion and Associates, architects, to design a new community center building at James Rolph Playground, Potrero Avenue at 26th and Hampshire Streets, for a fee of $16,000.
The Recreation and Park Commission awarded the contract to build the recreation building at James Rolph Playground to Nibbi Bros. at $349,800.

A sundial in memory of Maurice J. Sweeney, a member of the Recreation Commission, was set to be dedicated at the playground on Sunday, August 2, 1942, after the Commission had refused a memorial plaque under its policy against plaques on playgrounds.
The Board of Supervisors bought the James Rolph Jr. Playground land for the Playground Commission.
The Art Commission gave final approval to three galvanized steel window grills by Jack Kamesar, installed at the Rolph Recreation Center at 26th and Hampshire Streets.
